chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abdul-A'la, the mawla of the family of Sam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We are reported in our presence from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates the 'House of Meat'.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying! Rather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The house in which people backbite one another and eat their brothers' flesh.' And my father (peace be upon him) was 'meat'-loving, and he passed away; and on the day he passed away, in the sleeve of the mother of his child, there were thirty dirhams for the meat.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'The House of Meat' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* corrects a common literalist misunderstanding of the phrase 'al-Bayt al-Lahm' by linking it to the idiom of 'eating the flesh' of others through backbiting (ghibah). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Prophet’s statement referred to the specific 'house' or context where this spiritual consumption occurred, rather than meat itself being disliked. The narration further grounds this teaching in the lived reality of the Ahl al-Bayt, noting that Imam Ali (AS) himself enjoyed meat and died with funds reserved for it, thereby refuting the notion of ascetic rejection of meat.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yusuf, from Zakariyya Bin Muhammad Al Azdy, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Saam who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We are reported to in our presence from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> having said that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Hates the house of the meat’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! But rather Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The house in which the people are backbiting and eating their (brothers’) meats, and my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was meat-loving , and he<sup>asws</sup> passed away, (and on) the day he<sup>asws</sup> passed away in a sleeve of a mother of his<sup>asws</sup> child were thirty Dirhams for (buying) the meat’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Zakariya ibn Muhammad al-Azdiy from ‘Abd al-‘A’la’ Mawla’ Ale Sam who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘We narrate among us that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Allah, most Blessed, most High, disliked the house of meat.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘They have lied. The Messenger of Allah spoke only about the house in which people backbite and eat people’s meat. My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, liked meat and on the day he passed away, there was thirty dirham in the sleeve of the mother of his child to buy meat.’”
